title: A sound at its recorded level draws its volume line near the top of its lane, as the audio mock does
goal: In the audio mock a sound playing at its recorded level has its volume line close to the top of its lane, so the line reads as full and the waveform sits under it. In the app the same sound draws its line about a third of the way down, because the top third is kept for turning a sound up past its recorded level. Bring the line to where the mock draws it while still letting a sound be turned up.
notes: Found auditing a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-s-and-its-wa (2026-11-11). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-audio.html ~462 yOfLevel(v)=90-clamp(v,0,1)*78 (v=1 at 12/100). App: Sources/Photonz/SoundLane.swift y(forGain:) squares the travel against AudioLevel.loudestGain (twice unity), so unity sits at 1-sqrt(.5)=29% of the usable height: 26.9pt down an 84pt lane (measured on the probe: lane 864-948, line at 891). Walks with level-line coordinates: a-sound-s-volume-line-*, a-sound-s-bend-handle-follows-the-hand-walk, a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-walk, fade-diamonds-and-level-points-look-like-the-mock-walk, a-sound-s-waveform-follows-its-level-walk.
acceptance: A sound at its recorded level draws its volume line within the top fifth of its lane, as video-audio.html places it (yOfLevel: 90 - 78 x level, out of 100)
A sound can still be turned up past its recorded level by dragging the line or with the panel, and the line shows it
Dragging the line still lands it under the pointer, and the walks that drag a volume line by point are updated and pass

log.note: owns these walks: a-sound-lane-is-as-tall-as-the-mock-walk, a-sound-s-bend-handle-follows-the-hand-walk, a-sound-s-volume-line-plain-clicks-walk, a-sound-s-volume-line-picks-and-shapes-walk, a-sound-s-volume-line-menus-alternate-walk, fade-diamonds-and-level-points-look-like-the-mock-walk, a-sound-s-waveform-follows-its-level-walk

Adversarial review before: a Final Cut editor expects the 0 dB line near the top of an audio clip with a thin band above for boost, which is what the mock's yOfLevel gives; the cost is a thin boost strip (4.5 pt for +6 dB), with the panel slider as the fine control. Chose the mock's straight line below the recorded level over keeping the old fader curve because the mock is the floor.

Built: SoundLaneShape.levelY/gain(atLevelY:) in PhotonzCore (tests SoundLevelLineHeightTests, written first), SoundLane.swift reads them. Measured on the probe: lane 864-948, line at 874 (10 pt = 12 of 100). Walks updated for the new height (891 -> 874, bend handle and lane drags) and the lane walk now also turns the sound up by dragging (+4.5 dB) and by the slider (+5 dB). 18 walks run, all green; Scripts/test.sh green. Looked at 1-dark, 3-turned-down, 4-turned-up, 5-panel-up and the side-by-side: line at the top of the waveform at 0 dB, lower and smaller waveform turned down, higher when turned up.
left rough: the boost strip is thin (about 1.3 dB per point when dragging up); in the audit's rough list, not filed since the slider covers fine boosts and nobody has hit it yet.

The volume line now sits where video-audio.html's yOfLevel puts it: recorded level 12 of 100 down the lane (10 pt of 84, measured on the probe), silence at 90, with the strip above for turning up to +6 dB. Change is in PhotonzCore SoundLaneShape.levelY/gain(atLevelY:), with tests written first, and SoundLane.swift uses it. The lane walk turns the sound down (-3 dB), up by drag (+4.5 dB) and up by the slider (+5 dB). 18 walks green, Scripts/test.sh green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-11-11-sound-volume-line-at-the-top.json
